extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, patent attorneys/agents, and Office of Enrollment and Discipline (OED) staff / disciplinary counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards governing imposition of reciprocal discipline (exclusion) by the USPTO pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, including notice, service, publication, duties while excluded, and reinstatement procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 (exclusion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, the Director may impose reciprocal discipline upon a respondent identical to discipline imposed by a State (here, disbarment by the Supreme Court of Pennsylvania); Respondent is excluded from the practice of patent, trademark and other non-patent matters before the USPTO for violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order provided an opportunity to file a response opposing reciprocal discipline based on one or more reasons in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1). In this case Respondent did not file a response and it was determined there was no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d), so exclusion was appropriate. "Respondent is excluded from the practice of patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters before the USPTO" (order item 1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Predicate violation: 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h) (disbarment as basis for USPTO exclusion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h) is predicated upon being disbarred on ethical grounds from the practice of law by a duly constituted authority of a State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order states the exclusion was "predicated upon being disbarred on ethical grounds from the practice of law by a duly constituted authority of a State." The Office applies § 11.804(h) when a state disciplinary decision results in disbarment (see Notice of Exclusion text).

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional-conduct findings by the disciplining state authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The Disciplinary Board of the Supreme Court of Pennsylvania found violations of Rules of Professional Conduct pertaining to: diligence; communication; safekeeping of property; meritorious claims and contentions; candor to the tribunal; committing a criminal act that reflects adversely on honesty, trustworthiness, or fitness; misconduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation; and failing to respond to disciplinary counsel's request under the Disciplinary Rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These specific state-law findings served as the factual and ethical basis for the Pennsylvania Supreme Court's disbarment, which in turn supported the USPTO's reciprocal discipline under § 11.24. The Order summarizes the Board's findings in the Notice of Exclusion text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity and time to respond to Notice and Order (procedural due process)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order provided Respondent an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing the imposition of reciprocal discipline identical to that imposed by the state court, based on one or more of the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order was sent by certified mail and delivered on January 20, 2023. Respondent's failure to file a response within the 40-day period was treated as absence of a genuine issue of material fact under § 11.24(d), supporting the imposition of reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding of no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a respondent fails to file a timely response to the Notice and Order, the OED Director may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and impose reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order states: "In light of Respondent's failure to file a response, it is hereby determined that there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and Respondent's exclusion... is the appropriate discipline." This illustrates the procedural effect of non-response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration of exclusion and reinstatement procedure (37 C.F.R. § 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Respondent shall remain excluded from the practice of patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the USPTO until the OED Director grants a petition requesting Respondent's reinstatement pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order explicitly ties the duration of exclusion to the successful filing and grant of a reinstatement petition under the regulation cited (order item 2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and public availability of disciplinary decision
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order at OED's electronic FOIA Reading Room and publish a Notice in the Official Gazette describing the exclusion, the respondent, registration number, and the predicate violation(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order item 3 directs electronic publication at http://foiadocuments.uspto.gov; item 4 instructs publication of a Notice of Exclusion in the Official Gazette and gives sample Notice text that includes respondent's name, registration number, the rule violated (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)), and the state disbarment reference. The Order also states disciplinary decisions are available at https://foiadocuments.uspto.gov/oed/.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to other disciplinary enforcement agencies and courts (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the state(s) where Respondent is admitted to practice, to courts where Respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order item 5 requires dissemination of the disciplinary information to relevant state agencies and courts as specified by § 11.59.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties of disciplined practitioner (37 C.F.R. § 11.58)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 following imposition of public discipline by the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order item 6 directs Respondent to comply with § 11.58; the Final Order does not restate the duties but incorporates them by reference (these duties concern obligations such as notifying clients, closing or transferring matters, and other post-discipline responsibilities as set forth in § 11.58).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from customer numbers and USPTO electronic accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO shall dissociate Respondent's name from any Customer Number(s) and USPTO verified Electronic System account(s), if any.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order item 7 directs administrative dissociation of the disciplined individual's USPTO-related accounts to prevent continued representation or access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of the Final Order (certificate of service)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order was mailed by first-class certified mail, return receipt requested, to the Respondent at the most recent address provided to the OED Director pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.11(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order includes a Certificate of Service attesting to compliance with mailing requirements, demonstrating the procedural step of providing the respondent with the Final Order via certified mail.
